docs.title: DataGEMS User Profiler Api
docs.text:
This is the documentation site for the DataGEMS User Profiler Api. The service is part of the wider DataGEMS platform. This is part of the overall platform documentation.

The User Profiler Api keeps a profile for each DataGEMS user: who they are, where they work, their ORCID research output and, most importantly, a set of interest keywords. The keywords come from two sources: the user's ORCID record, and the natural language queries they ran on the platform, from which an LLM extracts the topics they care about. Session keywords age over time, so recent interests weigh more than old ones.

Other DataGEMS services read a trimmed, portable version of the profile to personalise what they offer. For example, the Query Recommender uses it to suggest the next queries:

GET /user/3f2e1d4c-.../profile
Authorization: Bearer <token>

{
  "userId": "3f2e1d4c-...",
  "keywords": ["knowledge graphs", "machine learning"],
  "weightedKeywords": [
    { "value": "knowledge graphs", "weight": 0.871, "source": "session" },
    { "value": "machine learning", "weight": 0.5, "source": "orcid" }
  ],
  "location": { "city": "Rome", "country": "Italy" },
  "affiliation": "CNR",
  "orcid": { "id": "0000-0002-1825-0097" }
}

You can use the menu options on the left to navigate through the available documentation. You may be interested to jump directly to an Architecture Overview, see the available Onboarding Material, read about some Api Constructs, investigate how to interpret Status & Error Codes or jump straight in to the OpenAPI Reference. You can find the repository for the service here: code repository.

For any questions, you can consult the FAQ, check if there is a relevant issue answering your question or contact the DataGEMS Help Desk.

docs.title: Api Overview
docs.text:
The service exposes an HTTP Api with JSON request and response bodies. In the DataGEMS development deployment it is reachable at https://datagems-dev.scayle.es/up.

The full, machine readable description is available in the OpenAPI Reference. A running instance also serves it at:

  • /api/v1/openapi.json: the OpenAPI document
  • /api/v1/swagger: Swagger UI
  • /api/v1/redoc: ReDoc

Note that the user endpoints are served at the root of the service (e.g. /users, /user/{user_id}), while the Api root and the auth test endpoint are under /api/v1.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Path Description GET /api/v1 Api root: confirms the Api is running. No authentication POST /api/v1/authtest Checks that a bearer token is accepted by the service GET /users Lists all users POST /user Creates a user, with a generated id POST /user/{user_id} Creates a user with a given id (e.g. the DMM one) GET /user/{user_id} Returns the full profile of a user PATCH /user/{user_id} Edits a user DELETE /user/{user_id} Deletes a user and everything connected to them GET /user/{user_id}/profile Returns the portable interest profile of a user GET /user/{user_id}/keywords Lists all keywords of a user with their current weight POST /user/{user_id}/keywords Appends session keywords to a user GET /user/{user_id}/generate-keywords Proposes keywords from the user's recent queries GET /user/{user_id}/queries_test Development: the user's queries as read from the DMM GET /orcid/{orcid_id} Returns a raw ORCID public record

All endpoints under /user/{user_id} answer 404 Not Found with {"detail": "No such user: '...'"} if the user does not exist.

docs.title: List users
docs.text:
GET /users

{
  "count": 2,
  "users": [
    { "userId": "3f2e1d4c-...", "name": "Alice", "surname": "Rossi" },
    { "userId": "a1b2c3d4-...", "name": "Bob", "surname": "Verdi" }
  ]
}

docs.title: Create a user
docs.text:
POST /user creates a user with a generated UUID and answers 201 Created with the full profile. POST /user/{user_id} does the same with the given id, which must be a lowercase, hyphenated UUID (otherwise 422), and answers 409 Conflict if a user with that id already exists. Use the latter to create the profile under the same id the DMM logs the user's queries with.

Only name, surname, email and affiliation are required:

{
  "name": "Alice",
  "surname": "Rossi",
  "email": "alice.rossi@example.com",
  "affiliation": "University of Milan"
}

A full body can also include the date of birth, initial session keywords, location, ORCID data and sessions:

{
  "name": "Bob",
  "surname": "Verdi",
  "dateOfBirth": "1984-05-12T00:00:00",
  "email": "bob.verdi@example.com",
  "affiliation": "CNR",
  "keywords": [{ "value": "knowledge graphs" }],
  "location": { "city": "Rome", "country": "Italy" },
  "orcid": {
    "id": "0000-0002-1825-0097",
    "keywords": [{ "value": "machine learning" }],
    "publications": [{
      "title": "Graph-Based User Profiling",
      "doi": "10.1000/xyz123",
      "journal": "Data Science Journal",
      "year": 2023,
      "authors": [{ "fullName": "Bob Verdi" }]
    }]
  },
  "sessions": [{
    "sessionId": "sess-001",
    "startTime": "2024-03-10T09:00:00",
    "endTime": "2024-03-10T09:45:00",
    "extracted": false,
    "queries": [
      { "text": "knowledge graph embedding", "typedAt": "2024-03-10T09:05:00" }
    ]
  }]
}

Unknown fields are ignored. Keywords without timestamps are stamped as seen at creation time.

docs.title: Retrieve a user
docs.text:
GET /user/{user_id} returns the full profile, as stored:

{
  "userId": "3f2e1d4c-...",
  "name": "Alice",
  "surname": "Rossi",
  "dateOfBirth": null,
  "email": "alice.rossi@example.com",
  "affiliation": "University of Milan",
  "keywords": [],
  "location": null,
  "orcid": null,
  "sessions": []
}

docs.title: Edit a user
docs.text:
PATCH /user/{user_id} changes only the fields present in the body and returns the updated profile. Nested objects and lists (location, orcid, sessions, keywords) are replaced as a whole: to add a session, fetch the profile, add it to the list, and send the full list back. Keywords that stay in the list keep their timestamps, new ones are stamped as seen now.

{ "affiliation": "CNR - Institute of Cognitive Sciences" }

To add keywords, prefer POST /user/{user_id}/keywords, which does not replace the existing ones.

docs.title: Delete a user
docs.text:
DELETE /user/{user_id} removes the user and all connected nodes (keywords, location, ORCID, publications, sessions and queries):

{ "message": "User '3f2e1d4c-...' deleted." }

docs.title: Interest profile
docs.text:
GET /user/{user_id}/profile

The portable profile meant for other services. It merges session and ORCID keywords into one de-duplicated list, strongest first, and leaves out expired keywords, personal data and the session log. See Keyword ageing.

{
  "userId": "3f2e1d4c-...",
  "keywords": ["knowledge graphs", "machine learning"],
  "weightedKeywords": [
    { "value": "knowledge graphs", "weight": 0.871, "source": "session" },
    { "value": "machine learning", "weight": 0.5, "source": "orcid" }
  ],
  "location": { "city": "Rome", "country": "Italy" },
  "affiliation": "CNR",
  "orcid": { "id": "0000-0002-1825-0097" }
}

keywords is a plain list, so consumers that ignore weights still get the priority order. weightedKeywords carries the weights and the source (session or orcid) of each one.

docs.title: List keywords with weights
docs.text:
GET /user/{user_id}/keywords returns all session and ORCID keywords with their current weight, strongest first, including expired ones:

{
  "keywords": [
    { "value": "GNN", "weight": 0.871, "source": "session", "lastSeenAt": "2026-09-25T10:00:00+00:00", "expired": false },
    { "value": "machine learning", "weight": 0.5, "source": "orcid", "lastSeenAt": null, "expired": false },
    { "value": "graphs", "weight": 0.06, "source": "session", "lastSeenAt": "2026-05-02T10:00:00+00:00", "expired": true }
  ]
}

docs.title: Generate keywords
docs.text:
GET /user/{user_id}/generate-keywords reads the user's latest queries from the DMM (up to 50 natural language and cross-dataset discovery queries) and asks the LLM for the keywords that describe them:

{ "keywords": ["knowledge graphs", "graph embedding", "GNN"] }

Nothing is saved: the result is a proposal, to be saved with POST /user/{user_id}/keywords. The endpoint returns {"keywords": []} without calling the LLM if the DMM has no queries for the user. It answers 502 Bad Gateway if the DMM or the LLM cannot be reached, if the DMM rejects the forwarded token, or if the LLM replies with invalid output.

The call can take a while, as it waits for both the DMM and the LLM. Clients should use a generous timeout.

docs.title: Append keywords
docs.text:
POST /user/{user_id}/keywords adds session keywords without touching the existing ones. A value already saved (ignoring case) is not duplicated: its lastSeenAt is refreshed, restoring its full weight.

{ "keywords": ["GNN", "knowledge graphs"] }

{ "added": ["GNN"], "refreshed": ["knowledge graphs"] }

docs.title: DMM queries (development)
docs.text:
GET /user/{user_id}/queries_test returns the queries the DMM has logged for the given user id, keyed by timestamp. It is the same lookup generate-keywords uses, exposed to check the DMM connection. The token must be accepted by the DMM too.

{
  "user_id": "ee01595a-ceec-4f54-8ece-f5e967f6036e",
  "count": 2,
  "queries": {
    "2026-10-20T09:12:44": "average rainfall in Lombardy",
    "2026-10-20T09:15:02": "rainfall datasets for northern Italy"
  }
}

docs.title: ORCID
docs.text: GET /orcid/{orcid_id} fetches the full public ORCID record for the given ORCID iD from the ORCID public Api and returns it unchanged. It is used by the Streamlit interface to fill in ORCID data when creating or editing a user. Nothing is saved.

docs.title: Auth test
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/authtest

Validates the caller's token (signature, issuer, expiry and audience) and echoes back the request and the identity found in the token. The request body has the same shape as the auth test endpoints of the other DataGEMS Apis, and no other fields are allowed:

{ "query": "test", "k": 1 }

{
  "authorized": true,
  "message": "Token is valid",
  "request": { "query": "test", "k": 1 },
  "subject": "the subject id",
  "username": "the preferred username"
}

docs.title: Api root
docs.text:
GET /api/v1 does not require authentication:

{ "message": "User Profiler API V1 is running" }

GET / redirects to it.

docs.title: Service Architecture
docs.text: The User Profiler is an HTTP Api written in Python with FastAPI and served by uvicorn. User profiles are stored as a property graph in an embedded Grafeo database that lives inside the service process, as described in Data Stores.

docs.title: Ecosystem
docs.text:
The service interacts with the following components:

  • DataGEMS AAI (Keycloak): issues the access tokens that callers present. The service downloads the realm's public keys (JWKS) to verify them. See Security.
  • Data Model Management (DMM): records the analytical patterns, and so the natural language queries, that users run on the platform. The service reads a user's recent queries from it to extract keywords.
  • LLM endpoint: an OpenAI-compatible chat completions Api (in the DataGEMS deployment, the one served at chat.scayle.es). It extracts keywords from the queries.
  • ORCID public Api: provides public researcher records, used to fill in ORCID data for a profile.
  • Consumers, such as the Query Recommender, which read the portable interest profile.
                         ┌──────────────────────┐
  client / consumer ───▶ │    User Profiler     │ ──── JWKS ──────▶ DataGEMS AAI (Keycloak)
  (Bearer token)         │        Api           │
                         │                      │ ── aplog search ─▶ DMM            (caller's token forwarded)
                         │  ┌────────────────┐  │ ── chat ─────────▶ LLM endpoint
                         │  │ Grafeo (graph) │  │ ── record ───────▶ ORCID public Api
                         │  └────────────────┘  │
                         └──────────────────────┘

docs.title: Data model
docs.text:
Each user is stored as a small subgraph, following the PG-schema in schema/user_model.pg:

User ──HAS_SESSION_KEYWORD──► Keyword          (session-extracted keywords)
     ──HAS_LOCATION─────────► Location
     ──HAS_ORCID────────────► ORCID ──HAS_KEYWORD─────► Keyword   (ORCID research keywords)
                                    ──HAS_PUBLICATION──► Publication ──HAS_AUTHOR──► Author
     ──HAS_SESSION──────────► Session ──HAS_QUERY──► Query
Node Properties User userId, name, surname, dateOfBirth (optional), email, affiliation Keyword value, addedAt and lastSeenAt (session keywords only) Location city, country ORCID id Publication title, doi, journal, year Author fullName Session sessionId, startTime, endTime (optional), extracted Query text, typedAt (optional)

The userId is a UUID. It is either generated by the service, or given by the caller so that it matches the id under which the DMM logs the user's queries.

docs.title: Keyword ageing
docs.text:
Session keywords carry two timestamps: addedAt, when the keyword was first saved, and lastSeenAt, the last time it was extracted from the user's queries. Their weight decays with the time since lastSeenAt:

weight = 0.5 ^ (days since lastSeenAt / KEYWORD_HALF_LIFE_DAYS)

So a keyword weighs 1.0 when just seen, 0.5 after one half-life (30 days by default), 0.25 after two, and so on. Extracting a keyword again refreshes lastSeenAt and restores its full weight, so recurring interests stay strong.

ORCID keywords have no timestamps and always weigh ORCID_KEYWORD_WEIGHT (0.5 by default). When the same value is both a session and an ORCID keyword (ignoring case), the higher weight is kept.

Keywords whose weight drops below KEYWORD_MIN_WEIGHT (0.1 by default, about 100 days with the default half-life) expire. They stay in the graph and are still listed by GET /user/{user_id} and GET /user/{user_id}/keywords, but the portable profile stops returning them, so other services no longer use them. Extracting them again brings them back.

The parameters are described in Configuration.

docs.title: Keyword extraction flow
docs.text:
Keywords are extracted in two steps, so that a person or a client can review them before they are saved:

  1. Propose. GET /user/{user_id}/generate-keywords reads the user's latest queries from the DMM (up to 50 natural language and cross-dataset discovery queries, using the caller's token) and asks the LLM for the relevant keywords. The reply is requested as JSON of the form {"keywords": [...]}, constrained with a JSON schema where the LLM endpoint supports it, then validated, trimmed and de-duplicated. Nothing is saved at this step.
  2. Save. POST /user/{user_id}/keywords appends the accepted keywords to the profile. Keywords already present are not duplicated: their lastSeenAt is refreshed instead.

docs.title: Portable interest profile
docs.text: GET /user/{user_id}/profile is the contract offered to other services. It returns only what is needed for personalisation: the active keywords, strongest first, as a plain list and with their weights and sources, plus location, affiliation and ORCID id. Personal data (email, dateOfBirth) and the raw session and query log are left out.

docs.title: Code layout
docs.text:
• up_api/main.py: the FastAPI application and all endpoints, including the DMM client
  • up_api/resources/security.py: token validation and the authtest endpoint
  • up_api/resources/graph_helpers.py: GQL utilities and the graph read / write operations
  • up_api/resources/profile_helpers.py: keyword weights, timestamps and the portable profile
  • up_api/resources/LLM_helpers.py: model selection, prompt, LLM call and reply validation
  • up_api/resources/orcid_helpers.py: ORCID public Api client
  • up_api/resources/data_models.py: the node models and request bodies
  • schema/user_model.pg: the PG-schema of the graph
  • examples/: end to end example scripts, in bash and PowerShell
  • app.py: a Streamlit user interface, described in Onboarding

docs.title: Automations
docs.text: A number of automations are available to facilitate the development, deployment and documentation of the service. Here we describe the ones that are directly, publicly available.

docs.title: Dockerfile
docs.text: The main delivery package for the service is a docker image. The Dockerfile at the root of the code repository builds the Docker image. Dependencies are installed with uv from the committed uv.lock, so the image always contains the exact dependency versions that were tested. Development tools, such as Streamlit, are left out of the image.

docs.title: Docker image publishing
docs.text:
A GitHub Action workflow is available to build and publish the docker image for the service. The action is triggered when a new tag matching v* is pushed to the repository. This way, all the images produced are always named and can be traced back to the codebase snapshot that generated them.

The generated docker image is pushed to the GitHub organization Packages using the name of the service repo and the version tag that triggered the execution.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
A GitHub Action workflow is available to generate the documentation presented here. The action is triggered manually and runs against the selected branch of the repository. The documentation generated is versioned and the documentation version is expected as input to the workflow.

The documentation is built using the mkdocs library and specifically using the Material for mkdocs theme. A number of additional tools are utilized, such as mike to support versioning and neoteroi.mkdocsoad to support OpenAPI specification rendering.

The documentation is generated and tagged with the provided version, which is also aliased as latest. It is pushed to the gh-pages branch, which the repository GitHub Page presents its contents from. The branch is created by the first run if it does not exist yet.

The OpenAPI Reference is rendered from the openapi.json file kept with the documentation. When the Api changes, this file should be refreshed from a running instance (/api/v1/openapi.json) before publishing a new documentation version.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: The service is configured entirely through environment variables. They are read once, when the service starts, so any change requires a restart.

docs.title: Data store
docs.text: Variable Default Description GRAFEO_DB_PATH ./grafeo_data Folder of the embedded Grafeo database holding all users. In Kubernetes it must be on a persistent volume, see Data Stores

docs.title: Keyword ageing
docs.text:
Variable Default Description KEYWORD_HALF_LIFE_DAYS 30 Days for a session keyword's weight to halve KEYWORD_MIN_WEIGHT 0.1 Below this weight a keyword expires and is left out of the portable profile (about 100 days with the default half-life) ORCID_KEYWORD_WEIGHT 0.5 Constant weight of ORCID keywords

See Keyword ageing.

docs.title: LLM
docs.text:
Variable Default Description LLM_API_URL (none) Full URL of the OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint, e.g. https://chat.scayle.es/api/chat/completions LLM_TOKEN (none) Bearer token used to call the LLM endpoint. This is a secret LLM_MODEL_LIST (none) URL listing the models available at the LLM endpoint, e.g. https://chat.scayle.es/api/models. If it is not set or cannot be reached, the preferred model name is used as is LLM_SSL_VERIFY true TLS certificate verification for the LLM endpoint. true verifies against the system CAs, a file path verifies against that CA bundle or certificate, false disables verification (for an endpoint with a self-signed certificate). With false, the service prints a warning at startup

The LLM is only needed by GET /user/{user_id}/generate-keywords. If these variables are not set, every other endpoint still works.

The preferred model is kimi-k2.6. The service checks it against the model list and falls back to the first available model if it is not offered. The preferred model is currently set in code, not through configuration.

docs.title: DMM
docs.text: Variable Default Description DMM_URL https://datagems-dev.scayle.es/dmm Base URL of the Data Model Management service, where the users' queries are read from. In the DataGEMS cluster this is http://data-model-management-service:5000 MOCK_DMM (unset) Development only. When set to 1, queries are read from a local mock_aplog.json file instead of the DMM

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Variable Default Description OIDC_ISSUER_URL https://datagems-dev.scayle.es/oauth/realms/dev The expected token issuer (iss claim), i.e. the DataGEMS AAI realm OIDC_JWKS_URL {OIDC_ISSUER_URL}/protocol/openid-connect/certs Where the issuer public keys are fetched from OIDC_CLIENT_ID user-profiler The client id of this service OIDC_ALLOWED_AUDIENCES {OIDC_CLIENT_ID},query-recommender Comma separated list of audiences: a token is accepted if its aud claim contains any of them JWKS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS 300 How long the public keys are cached, in seconds

See Security for how these are used.

docs.title: Http
docs.text:
Variable Default Description ROOT_PATH (empty) The path prefix under which a reverse proxy exposes the service, e.g. /up. It is used so that the generated OpenAPI document and the Swagger UI work behind the proxy. The proxy is expected to strip the prefix before forwarding requests

The Docker image listens on port 5000. When started locally with uvicorn up_api.main:app, the default port is 8000.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
export LLM_API_URL="https://chat.scayle.es/api/chat/completions"
export LLM_MODEL_LIST="https://chat.scayle.es/api/models"
export LLM_TOKEN="your-llm-token"
uvicorn up_api.main:app --reload

$env:LLM_API_URL = "https://chat.scayle.es/api/chat/completions"
$env:LLM_MODEL_LIST = "https://chat.scayle.es/api/models"
$env:LLM_TOKEN = "your-llm-token"
uvicorn up_api.main:app --reload

When working against an LLM endpoint with a self-signed certificate, save the endpoint's certificate once and point LLM_SSL_VERIFY to it, rather than disabling verification:

openssl s_client -connect <llm-host>:<port> </dev/null 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 > llm.pem
export LLM_SSL_VERIFY="$PWD/llm.pem"

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: LLM_TOKEN is the only secret the service needs. It should not be stored alongside the other configuration values. In the DataGEMS deployment it is kept in Vault and exposed to the container through a Kubernetes secret, as described in Deployment.

docs.title: Data Stores
docs.text: The service is the owner of the DataGEMS user profiles, so unlike a pure gateway it keeps state of its own.

docs.title: Graph database
docs.text:
Profiles are stored in Grafeo, an embedded property graph database queried with GQL. "Embedded" means the database runs inside the service process and keeps its data in a local folder, set with GRAFEO_DB_PATH (./grafeo_data by default). There is no separate database server to run.

The structure of the graph is defined by the PG-schema in schema/user_model.pg and summarised in the Architecture.

The database is opened when the service starts and flushed and closed when it shuts down, for example when Kubernetes stops the pod.

docs.title: Persistence
docs.text:
As the data lives in a local folder, that folder must survive restarts. In Kubernetes it must be on a persistent volume: the DataGEMS deployment mounts the user-profiler-pvc volume on /data and sets GRAFEO_DB_PATH=/data/grafeo_data. Without a persistent volume, every redeploy starts with no users.

Because only one process can safely use the database folder at a time, the service must run as a single replica, and updates must stop the old pod before starting the new one (the Recreate deployment strategy). See Deployment.

docs.title: How profiles are written
docs.text: Writes rewrite the whole user subgraph: the existing User node and everything connected to it is deleted, then the updated profile is written again. This keeps the graph consistent with the profile model, but means that two concurrent writes to the same user can overwrite each other: the last one wins.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: The service is part of the DataGEMS platform offered through an existing deployment, following the DataGEMS release and deployment procedures over a managed infrastructure. The purpose of this section is not to detail the deployment processes put in place by the DataGEMS team, but to give an overview of what the service needs to run.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
The service is offered as a Docker image through the DataGEMS GitHub Organization Packages, as ghcr.io/datagems-eosc/datagems-eosc/user-profiler:<version>. This process is described in the relevant Automations section.

The image is based on python:3.12-slim, installs the locked dependencies with uv (without the development tools, such as Streamlit) and starts the Api with uvicorn on port 5000. Mount a volume for the database folder, otherwise the users are lost when the container is removed:

docker run -p 5000:5000 \
  -v user-profiler-data:/data \
  -e GRAFEO_DB_PATH=/data/grafeo_data \
  -e LLM_API_URL="https://chat.scayle.es/api/chat/completions" \
  -e LLM_MODEL_LIST="https://chat.scayle.es/api/models" \
  -e LLM_TOKEN="your-llm-token" \
  ghcr.io/datagems-eosc/datagems-eosc/user-profiler:<version>

docs.title: Kubernetes
docs.text:
In the DataGEMS development cluster the service runs in the univr namespace, as:

  • a Deployment user-profiler with a single replica and the Recreate strategy, as the embedded database can only be used by one process at a time (see Data Stores). It has a readiness probe on TCP port 5000 and resource limits of 500m CPU and 2Gi memory
  • a PersistentVolumeClaim user-profiler-pvc, mounted on /data, holding the database (GRAFEO_DB_PATH=/data/grafeo_data)
  • a ClusterIP Service user-profiler-service on port 5000, which is how other services in the cluster, such as the Query Recommender, reach it
  • an Ingress and an HTTPRoute exposing https://datagems-dev.scayle.es/up/..., stripping the /up prefix (ROOT_PATH is set to /up accordingly), with request timeouts raised to 300 seconds to leave room for keyword generation
  • a VaultStaticSecret that syncs the LLM_TOKEN from Vault into the user-profiler-secrets Kubernetes secret

The manifests are maintained in the deployment repository of the service.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: In order for the service to operate properly, the needed configuration values must be set to match the environment that it must operate in. The needed configuration is described in the relevant Configuration section.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
For the service to be able to operate, its underpinning services must be available and accessible:

  • the DataGEMS AAI, to verify tokens. Without it, authenticated calls fail with 503
  • a persistent volume for the database. Without it, users are lost at every redeploy
  • the DMM and the LLM endpoint, to generate keywords. Without them, keyword generation fails with 502, while every other endpoint keeps working
  • the ORCID public Api, to fetch ORCID records. Only GET /orcid/{orcid_id} depends on it

The Architecture section describes the ecosystem in which the service needs to operate.

docs.title: Status & Error Codes
docs.text:
The HTTP Api exposed by the service exposes restful endpoints to offer its functionality. These endpoints are documented using the OpenAPI specification and available for integrators to consult in the respective API section.

In this section, we describe further the HTTP Status Codes that the service may return and the error information that accompanies them.

docs.title: Status Codes
docs.text:
The service makes use of the following subset of HTTP Status Codes:

  • 200 OK - the request has succeeded
  • 201 Created - the user was created
  • 401 Unauthorized - the request lacks valid authentication credentials: the token is missing, malformed, expired, has an invalid signature or was issued by another issuer
  • 403 Forbidden - the token is valid, but none of its audiences is allowed for this service
  • 404 Not Found - the user, or the ORCID record, does not exist
  • 409 Conflict - a user with the given id already exists
  • 422 Unprocessable Content - the request does not match the expected model, or a given user id is not a valid UUID
  • 502 Bad Gateway - an underpinning service (DMM or LLM) could not be reached, returned an error, or replied with unexpected output
  • 503 Service Unavailable - the public keys needed to verify the token could not be fetched from the identity provider
  • 500 Internal Server Error - an unexpected condition prevented the service from fulfilling the request

Authentication is checked first, so a request with a bad token gets a 401 or 403 regardless of anything else in it.

Errors returned by the ORCID public Api, other than 404, are passed on with the same status code.

docs.title: Error responses
docs.text:
Error responses follow the standard FastAPI format: a JSON object with a detail property. For all status codes except 422 caused by the request body, detail is a human readable message:

Status detail Cause 401 Missing bearer token No Authorization: Bearer header 401 Invalid token Bad signature, wrong issuer, expired or malformed token 403 Token missing required audience: one of user-profiler, query-recommender No allowed audience in the token 404 No such user: '<user_id>' Unknown user 404 ORCID profile not found: '<orcid_id>' Unknown ORCID iD 409 User '<user_id>' already exists POST /user/{user_id} with an id already in use 422 user_id must be a lowercase, hyphenated UUID POST /user/{user_id} with an invalid id 502 The DMM could not be reached: ... Network error towards the DMM 502 The DMM returned <status>: ... The DMM answered with an error, e.g. 401/403 if it rejects the forwarded token 502 The DMM returned an unexpected response The DMM reply could not be parsed 502 The LLM could not be reached or returned an invalid response The LLM call failed or its reply could not be parsed 503 Could not fetch JWKS: ... The identity provider public keys are not reachable

For example:

{
    "detail": "No such user: '3f2e1d4c-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'"
}

docs.title: Validation errors
docs.text:
When the request body does not match the expected model, detail is a list with one entry per problem found. Each entry has a loc pointing at the problematic property, a msg describing the problem, a machine friendly type and the input that was received.

For example, creating a user without an email:

{
    "detail": [
        {
            "type": "missing",
            "loc": ["body", "email"],
            "msg": "Field required",
            "input": { "name": "Alice", "surname": "Rossi", "affiliation": "University of Milan" }
        }
    ]
}

docs.title: Bad Gateway
docs.text: A 502 means the request was valid and authenticated, but an underpinning service needed to serve it did not work as expected. It only concerns generate-keywords and queries_test, which depend on the DMM and, for the former, the LLM. For the DMM, the detail includes the status code it returned, which helps telling a rejected token (401/403) from an outage. For the LLM, the exact cause is logged by the service (see Logging) but not returned to the caller. As LLM replies vary between calls, retrying may succeed.

docs.title: What is the difference between /user/{user_id} and /user/{user_id}/profile?
docs.text: /user/{user_id} returns everything the service stores about the user, including personal data and the session log. /user/{user_id}/profile is the portable profile meant for other services: active keywords ranked by weight, location, affiliation and ORCID id only. Services that personalise their behaviour should use the latter.

docs.title: Why did a keyword disappear from the profile?
docs.text: Its weight dropped below KEYWORD_MIN_WEIGHT because it was not seen for a long time (about 100 days with the default settings). It is still stored and listed by /user/{user_id}/keywords with "expired": true, and comes back if it is extracted again. See Keyword ageing.

docs.title: Why doesn't keyword generation save anything?
docs.text: On purpose: generate-keywords only proposes keywords, so they can be reviewed first. Save the ones you want with POST /user/{user_id}/keywords.

docs.title: Keyword generation always returns an empty list
docs.text: The DMM has no queries logged under that user id. Profiles must be created with the same id the DMM uses for the user (POST /user/{user_id}). The queries_test endpoint, or the DMM queries tab of the Streamlit interface, shows what the DMM has for a given id.

docs.title: Keyword generation fails with "The DMM returned 401"
docs.text: Your token is not accepted by the DMM. As the service forwards your token to the DMM, it needs the DMM audience as well as this service's.

docs.title: Should I use PATCH to add keywords?
docs.text: No. PATCH /user/{user_id} replaces the whole keyword list. Use POST /user/{user_id}/keywords, which appends new keywords and refreshes the existing ones.

docs.title: Can I run more than one replica?
docs.text: No. The embedded database can only be used by one process at a time, so the service must run as a single replica. See Data Stores.

docs.title: Known Issues
docs.text:
• There are no per-user permissions: any accepted token can read and change any profile. See Security.
  • Writes rewrite the whole user subgraph, so concurrent writes to the same user can overwrite each other.
  • query-recommender is accepted as an audience as a temporary workaround, until the DataGEMS Keycloak configuration adds user-profiler to the tokens the Query Recommender forwards.
  • The user endpoints are served at the root of the service rather than under /api/v1, unlike the Api root and the auth test endpoint.
  • GET / redirects to /api/v1 without taking the proxy prefix into account. Behind the DataGEMS ingress, use /up/api/v1 directly.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: The service writes its logs to standard output, where they are collected by the container runtime. In the DataGEMS cluster they can be read with the usual Kubernetes tooling, e.g. kubectl logs -n univr deployment/user-profiler.

docs.title: Access logs
docs.text:
Each request served is logged by uvicorn in its standard access log format, with the client address, method, path and status code:

INFO:     10.0.0.12:53124 - "GET /user/3f2e1d4c-.../profile HTTP/1.1" 200 OK

docs.title: Troubleshooting logs
docs.text:
The service logs the conditions that are hidden from the caller behind a generic error, or handled without failing the request:

Message Meaning JWT validation failed: ... A token was rejected (401). The message gives the reason, e.g. an expired signature Could not reach models endpoint: ... The list of available LLM models could not be fetched, so the preferred model name was used as is Error while calling API: ... The LLM call failed (502 to the caller) LLM reply contains no JSON object: ... The LLM replied without any JSON (502 to the caller). The reply is included LLM reply does not match the expected schema: ... The LLM replied with JSON of the wrong shape (502 to the caller) WARNING: TLS certificate verification for the LLM API is disabled ... Printed at startup when LLM_SSL_VERIFY=false

DMM errors are not logged separately, as their details are returned to the caller in the 502 response, see Status & Error Codes.

The service does not currently produce structured (JSON) logs, propagate a correlation identifier, or emit accounting entries.

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text: The service is part of the DataGEMS platform offered through an existing deployment, following the DataGEMS release and deployment procedures over a managed infrastructure along with the maintenance activities that are scheduled within the platform. The purpose of this section is not to detail the maintenance activities put in place by the DataGEMS team.

docs.title: Healthchecks
docs.text:
The Api root, GET /api/v1, does not require authentication and answers 200 OK as soon as the service is up. It can be used as a liveness check:

curl https://datagems-dev.scayle.es/up/api/v1

{ "message": "User Profiler API V1 is running" }

This check does not cover the database or the underpinning services. To also verify authentication and the database end to end, call GET /users with a valid token. To verify the DMM connection, use GET /user/{user_id}/queries_test.

In Kubernetes, the readiness of the container is checked with a TCP probe on port 5000.

docs.title: Versions & Updates
docs.text:
The service follows a semantic versioning scheme and structures versions as MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH:

  • MAJOR (X.0.0): Breaking changes that are incompatible with previous versions.
  • MINOR (X.Y.0): New features added in a backward-compatible way.
  • PATCH (X.Y.Z): Bug fixes and security patches that do not affect compatibility.

Each version is released by pushing a vX.Y.Z tag, which builds and publishes the matching Docker image, as described in Automations.

Keywords saved by older versions, before keyword timestamps existed, are stamped the next time the user's profile is saved.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text:
All state is kept in the Grafeo database folder (GRAFEO_DB_PATH), as described in Data Stores. Backing up the service means copying that folder. To get a consistent copy, take it while the service is stopped, or from a snapshot of the persistent volume.

To keep backups of the state, the copy must be scheduled to run in a consistent manner.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Troubleshooting is primarily done through the logs, described in the respective logging section. Common symptoms and their usual causes are:

  • 401 on every call: the token is expired, or was issued by a different realm than OIDC_ISSUER_URL
  • 403 on every call: the token audience contains neither user-profiler nor query-recommender
  • All users disappear after a redeploy: GRAFEO_DB_PATH is not on a persistent volume
  • Keyword generation answers 502 with The DMM returned 401 or 403: the token is not accepted by the DMM. It needs the DMM audience as well
  • Keyword generation answers 502 with the LLM message: the LLM endpoint is unreachable, LLM_TOKEN is wrong, or TLS verification is failing (look for CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED in the logs)
  • Keyword generation always returns an empty list: the DMM has no queries for that user id. Check that the profile was created with the same id the DMM logs the user under

docs.title: Onboarding Material
docs.text: This section contains some references and material that will assist users and integrators onboarding process.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
The definite guide for integrators remains the service OpenAPI Reference.

The codebase is available under the MIT License in our GitHub code repository.

To get a better understanding of the endpoints and their payloads, you can read the Api Overview.

To know more about Api response codes and how to interpret them, you can take a look at the Status & Error Codes.

On aspects pertaining to security, you can read more at the Security section.

For an overall view of the service, you can go through the Architecture.

For any questions, you can consult the FAQ.

If you are facing a problem, check if there is a relevant issue answering your question.

You can always contact us through the DataGEMS Help Desk.

docs.title: Running locally
docs.text:
The service requires Python 3.12 or later. With uv:

git clone https://github.com/datagems-eosc/user-profiler.git
cd user-profiler
uv sync
uv run uvicorn up_api.main:app --reload

The Api is then available at http://localhost:8000, with the Swagger UI at http://localhost:8000/api/v1/swagger. The database is created in ./grafeo_data. To use keyword generation, set the LLM and DMM variables described in Configuration.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Ready-to-run scripts that exercise the endpoints end to end are in the examples folder of the code repository, for bash (api_examples.sh) and PowerShell (api_examples.ps1). They start from an empty database, create two users, run through the operations, and delete both users so the database is clean at the end.

bash examples/api_examples.sh

.\examples\api_examples.ps1

All endpoints except the Api root need an Authorization: Bearer <token> header, with an access token retrieved from the DataGEMS AAI service with user-profiler (or query-recommender) in its audience. For example:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" http://localhost:8000/users

docs.title: User interface
docs.text:
The code repository includes a Streamlit interface, app.py, for interactive use:

uv sync                      # Streamlit is a development dependency
uv run streamlit run app.py

In the sidebar you choose the Api to use (local, the DataGEMS development instance, or local with DMM mode) and paste the Keycloak access token, which can also be provided through the DATAGEMS_TOKEN environment variable. The interface warns when the token is missing or expired.

It has three tabs:

  • Users: list, create, edit and delete users. When creating or editing a user, ORCID data can be fetched from ORCID by iD. A user's page shows their location, keywords, ORCID data and sessions, and lets you generate keywords and Accept & save the new ones
  • Chat: pick a user and type queries as they would. Queries are recorded in a session, which is closed after 5 minutes of inactivity
  • DMM queries: look up the queries the DMM has logged for a user id, or the most recent queries by any user. Useful to find which user id a query was logged under

docs.title: Quality Assurance
docs.text: Key aspects of the Quality Assurance checklist that DataGEMS services must pass have been defined in the processes and documents governing the platform development and quality assurance. In this section we present a selected subset of these that are directly, publicly available.

docs.title: Reproducible builds
docs.text: The service dependencies are pinned in the uv.lock file of the code repository, and the Docker image is built from that lock file (uv sync --frozen). Every published image is tagged with the version tag of the commit it was built from. See Automations.

docs.title: Input handling
docs.text: All request bodies are validated against their models before they reach the database. Values written to the graph are escaped before being placed in GQL queries, so that user supplied text cannot alter the queries. User ids given by callers must be canonical UUIDs.

docs.title: Output validation
docs.text: As keywords are produced by an LLM, the service does not trust its output. The LLM is asked to reply in a fixed JSON format, constrained with a JSON schema where the endpoint supports it. Every reply is then validated against that format, and the keywords are trimmed and de-duplicated before being returned. Replies that cannot be validated are reported to the caller as a 502 instead of being passed on. Generated keywords are only proposals: they are saved only when explicitly appended to the profile.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
The end to end example scripts in the examples folder exercise the endpoints against a local or deployed instance, starting from and returning to an empty database. They can be used as a smoke test, as shown in Onboarding.

The Streamlit interface described in Onboarding can be used for manual, end to end testing, including the DMM and LLM integration.

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Key aspects of the Security checklist and practices that DataGEMS services must pass have been defined in the processes and documents governing the platform development and quality assurance. In this section we present a selected subset of these that are directly, publicly available and affect the usage and configuration of the service.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All endpoints except the Api root (GET /api/v1) and the OpenAPI documentation require authentication using Bearer tokens in the form of JWTs (JSON Web Tokens). Clients must include a valid token in the Authorization header of each HTTP request, using the following format:

Authorization: Bearer <token>

The service only accepts JWTs issued by the trusted identity provider, the DataGEMS AAI service. When a token is received, the service:

  1. verifies the token signature with the public keys (JWKS) published by the issuer. Only RS256 signatures are accepted
  2. checks that the issuer iss claim matches the configured DataGEMS AAI realm
  3. checks the expiration exp claim, to confirm the token is still valid
  4. checks that the audience aud claim contains at least one of the allowed audiences. aud can be either a single string or a list

By default the allowed audiences are user-profiler and query-recommender. The second one is there because the Query Recommender forwards its caller's token to this service, and the DataGEMS Keycloak configuration does not add user-profiler to those tokens yet. It can be removed, through OIDC_ALLOWED_AUDIENCES, once it does.

Only if all these checks pass will the request be processed. A missing or invalid token results in 401 Unauthorized, while a valid token issued for another service results in 403 Forbidden. If the public keys cannot be fetched from the issuer, the service answers 503 Service Unavailable. See Status & Error Codes.

The public keys are cached in memory for 5 minutes by default, so a key rotation at the issuer can take up to that long to be picked up.

You can check that a token is accepted by calling the POST /api/v1/authtest endpoint, described in the Api Overview.

The location of the configuration governing this behaviour is described in the relevant Configuration section.

docs.title: Authorization
docs.text: There are currently no per-user permissions within the service. Any caller presenting a valid token with an allowed audience can read, create, edit and delete any profile. Access to the service should therefore be limited to trusted DataGEMS clients and services.

docs.title: Personal data
docs.text: Full profiles (GET /user/{user_id}) include personal data, such as email and date of birth, and the user's query log. Services that only need to personalise their behaviour should use the portable profile (GET /user/{user_id}/profile), which leaves these out.

docs.title: Calls to other services
docs.text:
To extract keywords, the service reads the user's queries from the DMM on behalf of the caller, by forwarding the caller's access token as is. There is no token exchange: the token must also be accepted by the DMM, so its audience must include the DMM as well. If the DMM rejects the token, keyword generation answers 502 with the DMM status code.

The caller's token is never sent to the LLM endpoint, which is called with a dedicated service token, nor to ORCID, whose public Api needs no authentication.

docs.title: TLS towards the LLM endpoint
docs.text: The service verifies the TLS certificate of the LLM endpoint against the system certificate authorities by default. This can be pointed to a specific CA bundle or certificate, or, for development against an endpoint with a self-signed certificate, disabled. Disabling verification prints a warning at startup. See Configuration.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: The LLM token is a secret and must be handled separately from the other configuration values. In the DataGEMS deployment it is kept in Vault and injected into the container as an environment variable. See Configuration and Deployment.
